Asturian

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈreta/ [ˈre.t̪a]
  • Rhymes: -eta
  • Syllabification: re‧ta

Verb

[edit]

reta

  1. inflection of retar:
    1. third-person singular present indicative
    2. second-person singular imperative

Esperanto

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From reto (“net”, noun) +‎ -a (adjectival suffix).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈreta/
  • Audio 1:(file)
  • Audio 2:(file)
  • Rhymes: -eta
  • Syllabification: re‧ta

Adjective

[edit]

reta (accusative singular retan, plural retaj, accusative plural retajn)

  1. net (in most senses, including mesh, tool for trapping, figurative, computing network, Internet)
    Reta Vortaro ― Internet Dictionary

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Malay harta, from Sanskrit अर्थ (artha).

Noun

[edit]

reta

  1. property
  2. wealth
  3. treasure

Derived terms

[edit]
  • bereta

Polish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Deverbal from ratować.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Masovia):
    • (Far Masovian) IPA(key): [ˈrɛ.ta]

Noun

[edit]

reta f

  1. (Far Masovian) synonym of ratunek

Further reading

[edit]
  • Antoni Waga (1860), “reta”, in “Abecadłowy spis wyrazów ludowego języka w okolicach Łomży, Wizny i przyległych”, in Kazimierz Władysław Wóycicki, editor, Biblioteka Warszawska‎[1] (in Polish), volume 2, Warsaw, page 757

Portuguese

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • recta (pre-1990 spelling)

Etymology

[edit]

From Latin rēcta, feminine of rēctus (“straight”), from perfect passive participle of regō (“to rule”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₃reǵ- (“to straighten, to direct”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈʁɛ.tɐ/ [ˈhɛ.tɐ]
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈʁɛ.tɐ/ [ˈhɛ.tɐ]
    • (Rio de Janeiro) IPA(key): /ˈʁɛ.tɐ/ [ˈχɛ.tɐ]
    • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈʁɛ.ta/ [ˈhɛ.ta]
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ˈʁɛ.tɐ/

  • Hyphenation: re‧ta

Adjective

[edit]

reta

  1. feminine singular of reto

Noun

[edit]

reta f (plural retas)

  1. (geometry) line (infinite one-dimensional figure)
  2. a straight section of a path or road
    Antonym: curva

Derived terms

[edit]
  • semirreta

Related terms

[edit]
  • retificar
  • reto

Further reading

[edit]
  • “reta”, in Dicionário Aulete Digital (in Portuguese), Rio de Janeiro: Lexikon Editora Digital, 2008–2026
  • “reta”, in Dicionário Priberam da Língua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Lisbon: Priberam, 2008–2026

Swedish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Old Norse reita, from Proto-Germanic *wraitijaną.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Sweden) IPA(key): /ˈrêː.ta/
  • Audio:(file)

Verb

[edit]

reta (present retar, preterite retade, supine retat, imperative reta)

  1. to tease
  2. to annoy or irritate or provoke; to make somebody or something irritated

Inflection

[edit]
Conjugation of reta (weak)
active passive
infinitive reta retas
supine retat retats
imperative reta —
imper. plural1 reten —
present past present past
indicative retar retade retas retades
ind. plural1 reta retade retas retades
subjunctive2 rete retade retes retades
present participle retande
past participle retad

1 Archaic. 2 Dated. See the appendix on Swedish verbs.

Derived terms

[edit]
  • retfull
  • retfullhet
  • retlig
  • retning
  • retsticka
  • skrattretande

Anagrams

[edit]
  • aret, erat, reat, trea
